text:
- [IARC.1.10] **Async-first, never depends on threads.**
  Load-bearing design invariant across every libds
  module, not just the consumption loop. libds
  **never** depends on threads for anything: no
  `pthread_*` calls, no `sleep` / `nanosleep`, no
  internally-spawned threads, no background timers,
  no thread-local state as a semantic mechanism, no
  locks held across a callback. The consumption loop
  exposes a pump function
  (`ds_engine_pump(engine)`) that runs to agenda
  exhaustion and returns ([NLFC.2.2]). Every other module —
  `dispatcher`, `recorder`, `wm` — is equally
  thread-free: they
  produce callbacks, consume callbacks, mutate state
  on the pump's call stack, and that is all.
  The integrator may freely use threads in their
  own code — e.g. running pump on a dedicated
  thread, or calling pump from a thread pool — but
  libds does not require them to, does not assume
  them, and does not spawn them. The design
  assumption is that integrators are comfortable
  with async programming; we do not ship sync-mode
  conveniences or thread wrappers.
  **Pure async-event deployment (no threads at all)
  is the primary target.** Any module design that
  forces threading — "this callback must run on a
  different thread," "this lock must be held across
  an await," "this operation blocks pending I/O" —
  is a design regression to flag and redesign. All
  blocking I/O goes through callbacks the
  integrator's runtime drives; libds never waits,
  never spawns, never sleeps.
